working_title: The boxes I thought I needed

exercise.instructions: You are going to read an article about a personal experience related to moving home. Six sentences have been removed from the article. Choose from the sentences A–G the one which fits each gap (37–42). There is one extra sentence which you do not need to use.
exercise.text_title: The boxes I thought I needed
exercise.passage_with_gaps:
When I first arrived at my new, smaller home, I was surrounded by boxes. Each one was labelled “keep”, but I couldn’t explain what many of them contained. (37) I quickly realised that “keeping everything” was not an option. The floor space was limited, and I needed to make some decisions.

One box, in particular, caught my attention. It was filled with old cables and chargers, things I had kept “just in case” but never used. (38) This box became a symbol of my habit of holding onto things without purpose. I realised that many of these items had been forgotten over time, tucked away in corners and cupboards.

Instead of simply throwing everything away, I heard about a local swap and repair event. (39) It seemed like a perfect opportunity to see if some of these items could find a new home. I decided to take several uncertain items there, hoping they might be useful to someone else.

At the event, I was surprised. An old lamp I thought nobody would want was eagerly taken by a young couple. (40) On the other hand, a small ornament I had little use for still held sentimental value and returned home with me. That was different from the lamp, which found a new purpose.

Back at home, I started to develop a rule for what deserved space. (41) However, I allowed myself to keep a few impractical objects for personal reasons. This new criterion was about balancing practicality with personal value.

The next day, I found a place for the ornament on a shelf. It was a small action, but it felt significant. (42) It was a reminder that not every decision had to be purely practical. It showed that I could change my relationship with possessions. I realised that the move was not just about reducing the number of things I owned but about understanding what truly mattered to me.

As I continued to unpack, I found myself questioning the purpose of each item. Some things were easy to let go of, while others required more thought. I began to see my possessions in a new light, not just as objects but as parts of my life story. Each decision to keep or discard was a step towards creating a home that reflected who I was becoming. The process was more than just physical; it was about emotional and personal growth. I started to appreciate the stories behind each item, whether they were to be kept or passed on. This reflection made the experience of moving into a smaller space more meaningful than I had anticipated. I realised that I had been holding onto things out of habit, not necessity, and that this move was an opportunity to redefine what I truly valued.

The sentence 'I realised that many of these items had been forgotten over time.' refers back to the box of unused cables and chargers, highlighting the narrator's habitual keeping.

questions.rationale: The sentence 'I decided to take several uncertain items there.' connects the narrator's decision to the introduction of the swap event as an alternative to disposal.

The sentence 'That was different from the lamp, which found a new purpose.' contrasts the sentimental value of the ornament with the practical use of the lamp, enhancing the narrative's theme of value.

questions.rationale: The sentence 'This new criterion was about balancing practicality with personal value.' fits the narrative's progression towards a more deliberate approach to possessions.
The sentence 'It showed that I could change my relationship with possessions.' reflects the narrator's changed behaviour and concludes the narrative with a personal insight.
